label: late-episode ramp amplified by unrewarded/S2 outcomes at D1, S1 at D2, low value
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_state == 2) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) * (action == 2) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.) ;; (phase != D1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.) ;; value * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20.)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 12 sits near -1 for most of the episode and ramps up toward the end (timing alone R^2 0.70). What is left over is mostly history effects whose size grows with that ramp: all terms are multiplied by exp((ep_trial-99)/20), and this is why the score beats the additive ceiling (all = 0.28). At D1 it is higher after an unrewarded trial, most of all an unrewarded S2 trial (a1 S2 u, a2 S2 u), and it is also raised after reaching S2 at all; after S1 trials it is lower. At GO it is higher after a rewarded S1 trial. At D2 it is higher when S1 is reached, more so when S1 came by a rare transition from a2. The model value adds a graded negative effect (lower value means higher n late in the episode). The upcoming choice, policy logit and trials from two back added little. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.56 (dev 0.56). The observed-only version without the value term gets test 0.42. No future variables are used.

issues: The headline score reproduces: the claimed 8 terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.564. Without value, test R^2 is 0.421.

The D1 claim 'higher after an unrewarded trial' is too broad. The D1 residual after a1 S1 u is -0.013, which is lower, and a2 S1 u is only +0.007. The raise is specific to S2-unrewarded trials (a1 S2 u +0.070, a2 S2 u +0.066). Scores agree: D1*S2u*ramp alone gets 0.237 test, D1*unrewarded alone 0.166. After the claimed terms are fitted, misses still over-predict D1 after a1 S1 u (-0.023).

The claim 'reaching S2 raises it in general' at D1 is false. D1 residual after a1 S2 r is -0.003 and after a2 S2 r is -0.006. The D1*(prev_state==2)*ramp term alone gets only 0.073 test. Its fitted weight is just making up for the overly broad unrewarded term.

The claimed value effect (lower value means higher n) does not hold on its own. value*ramp alone gives test R^2 0.0025. value per phase gives 0.0024. The value-decile residuals are not monotonic: decile 0 is +0.012/+0.020 and deciles 7-8 at D1 are positive. The value term earns its 0.14 only alongside the other terms, partly because the term set has no plain ramp: (phase != D1)*ramp replaces one. Adding a plain ramp term to the 7 non-value terms gives 0.487, so value's real added share is about 0.08. Value is also a model output, not an observed cue.
The ramp shape is not tuned. exp((t-99)/10) beats /20: 0.565 vs 0.542 with the same corrected term set.

About 44% of the variance beyond timing is still unexplained, and the worst-fit windows are systematic. In late-episode streaks of repeated a1 -> S1 trials (t93-99), GO and D2 are under-predicted by about 0.15-0.25 in absolute value (e.g. D2 S1c actual -0.34 vs predicted -0.61). Repeat-S1 streak, prev-action, good-state and policy-logit terms did not close this gap (+0.00 to +0.01).
